items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: A randomized binary trial: independent and identically distributed subjects \(i=1,\ldots,n\), each carrying binary potential outcomes \(Y_i(0),Y_i(1)\in\{0,1\}\) and an independent Bernoulli\((p)\) assignment \(W_i\), with observed outcome \(Y_i=W_iY_i(1)+(1-W_i)Y_i(0)\). The private record \(X_i=(W_i,Y_i)\) takes values in the four-point alphabet \(\mathcal X=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\) with law \(\pi_\theta=(q(1-\mu_0),q\mu_0,p(1-\mu_1),p\mu_1)\), \(\theta=(\mu_0,\mu_1)\in(0,1)^2\), and the target is \(\tau=c^\top\theta=\mu_1-\mu_0\).

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: Local differential privacy with likelihood-ratio bound \(r=e^\varepsilon\) and \(d=r-1\), fixed \(\varepsilon>0\). A stationary channel \(Q\) is a Markov kernel from \(\mathcal X\) to an arbitrary measurable space satisfying \(Q(A\mid x)\le e^\varepsilon Q(A\mid x')\). A sequential protocol consists of Markov kernels \(Q_i\) from \(\mathcal X\times\prod_{j<i}\mathcal Z_j\) to \((\mathcal Z_i,\mathcal G_i)\) satisfying the same bound for every realized history \(H_{i-1}\). \(I_\theta(Q)\) is the Fisher information of the induced output experiment, and \(\kappa(Q)\) counts its active outputs.

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl: The finite staircase program: the fourteen nonconstant patterns \(S_1,\ldots,S_{14}\) (the bit-support of \(j\)), rays \(b_S=\mathbf1+d\mathbf1_S\), masses \(h_S(\theta)=\pi_\theta^\top b_S\), derivatives \(g_S\), the polytope \(\mathcal A_\varepsilon=\{\alpha\ge0:B\alpha=\mathbf1\}\), channels \(Q_\alpha(S\mid x_j)=\alpha_Sb_S(j)\), information \(I_\theta(\alpha)=\sum_S\alpha_Sg_Sg_S^\top/h_S(\theta)\), directions \(v(t)=(t,t+1)^\top\), the objective \(F_\theta(\alpha,t)\), and \(J^*=\max_\alpha\min_tF_\theta\), \(V^*=1/J^*\), together with the certified regions \(\mathcal R_3,\mathcal R_5\).

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: Local asymptotics at an interior point \(\theta_0\): alternatives \(\theta_{n,h}=\theta_0+h/\sqrt n\) with \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,H}(\theta_0)\), sequential private procedures \(\mathcal P=((Q^{(n)},\widehat\tau_n))_{n\ge1}\) with scaled errors \(U^{\mathcal P}_{n,h}=\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-c^\top\theta_{n,h})\), the regular class \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{reg}}_\varepsilon(\theta_0)\) with common limit law \(L_{\mathcal P}\) and uniformly integrable squared errors, the Wald level \(\gamma\) with critical value \(z_{1-\gamma/2}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\gamma/2)\), and the scalar van Trees handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{VT}}\).

items.label: Setup S-5
items.nl: The private-pilot procedure: a pilot of size \(m_n\) released by four-category randomized response gives \(\widetilde\theta\). A measurable saddle \((\widetilde\alpha,\widetilde t,\widetilde J)\) at \(\widetilde\theta\) is then selected, and the remaining \(n-m_n\) records are released through \(Q_{\widetilde\alpha}\). The estimator is \(\widehat\tau^*=c^\top\widetilde\theta+(n-m_n)^{-1}\sum_{i>m_n}\widetilde\phi(S_i)\), with variance estimator \(\widehat V^*\).

items.label: Setup S-6
items.nl: The published Ohnishi--Awan comparator: \(\widetilde A_i=W_iY_i/p-(1-W_i)Y_i/q+L_i\) with independent \(L_i\sim\operatorname{Lap}(0,\Delta_A/\varepsilon)\), \(\Delta_A=1/(pq)\), sample mean \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{OA}}\), and variance constant \(V_{\mathrm{OA}}=\mu_1/p+\mu_0/q-\tau^2+2\Delta_A^2/\varepsilon^2\).

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl: \(\mathfrak Q^{\mathrm{seq}}_{n,\varepsilon}\) is the set of \(n\)-stage protocols \(Q^{(n)}=(Q_i)_{i=1}^n\) on arbitrary measurable output spaces \((\mathcal Z_i,\mathcal G_i)\), where each \(Q_i(\cdot\mid x,h)\) is a Markov kernel from \(\mathcal X\times\prod_{j<i}\mathcal Z_j\) to \((\mathcal Z_i,\mathcal G_i)\), is nonanticipating, and satisfies \(Q_i(A\mid x,h)\le e^\varepsilon Q_i(A\mid x',h)\) for every \(A\in\mathcal G_i\), \(x,x'\in\mathcal X\), and history \(h\in\prod_{j<i}\mathcal Z_j\)

items.label: Definition P-4
items.nl: Using the fixed enumeration \(S_1,\ldots,S_{14}\), \(\mathcal R_3\) is the parameter set admitting primal normalization, profiling stationarity, active dual equalities, and strict inactive dual inequalities with active set \(\{S_1,S_6,S_8\}\). The region \(\mathcal R_5\) is the analogous set with active set \(\{S_3,S_4,S_6,S_8,S_9\}\), together with \(\rho_S(\theta,t)\ne\rho_T(\theta,t)\) for every two distinct \(S,T\in\{S_3,S_4,S_6,S_8,S_9\}\)

items.label: Definition P-5
items.nl: For \(R>0\), define \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{VT}}=(v(t^*),w_R)\), where \(t^*\) is a minimizing selection supplied by \(\mathrm{thm{:}finite\text{-}oracle}\), equivalently \(\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_\varepsilon}F_\theta(\alpha,t^*)=J^*(\theta,p,\varepsilon)\), and \(w_R=\operatorname{smoothPrior}(0,R)\). The conditional-score martingale and uniform domination over sequential procedures are proof obligations of \(\mathrm{thm{:}sequential\text{-}minimax}\), not fields of \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{VT}}\).

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl: Fix an arbitrary measurable strong-saddle selector: a measurable map that, for every interior \(\vartheta\), returns \((\alpha_{\vartheta},t_{\vartheta},J_{\vartheta})\) with \(\alpha_{\vartheta}\in\mathcal A_\varepsilon\), \(t_{\vartheta}\in\arg\min_t F_{\vartheta}(\alpha_{\vartheta},t)\), \(J_{\vartheta}=F_{\vartheta}(\alpha_{\vartheta},t_{\vartheta})=J^*(\vartheta,p,\varepsilon)\), and \(F_{\vartheta}(\alpha,t_{\vartheta})\le J_{\vartheta}\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathcal A_\varepsilon\). Profiling stationarity at \(t_{\vartheta}\) follows from the selected minimizer. Use an \(m_n\)-subject four-category randomized-response pilot with releases \(R_1,\ldots,R_{m_n}\). Define \(\widehat u_k=m_n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{m_n}\mathbf 1\{R_i=k\}\), \(\widehat\pi_k=\{(\exp(\varepsilon)+3)\widehat u_k-1\}/(\exp(\varepsilon)-1)\), and \(\delta_n=(m_n+2)^{-1}\), then set \(\widetilde\theta_0=\max\{\delta_n,\min\{1-\delta_n,\widehat\pi_1/(1-p)\}\}\) and \(\widetilde\theta_1=\max\{\delta_n,\min\{1-\delta_n,\widehat\pi_3/p\}\}\). Apply this selector to obtain \((\widetilde\alpha,\widetilde t,\widetilde J)\), release the remaining records through \(Q_{\widetilde\alpha}\), and set \(\widehat\tau^*=c^{\top}\widetilde\theta+(n-m_n)^{-1}\sum_{i=m_n+1}^n g_{S_i}^{\top}v(\widetilde t)/(\widetilde J h_{S_i}(\widetilde\theta))\).

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl: \(\widetilde A_i=W_iY_i/p-(1-W_i)Y_i/q+L_i\), where the \(L_i\) are iid \(\operatorname{Lap}(0,\Delta_A/\varepsilon)\) and independent of all subject records, \(\Delta_A=p^{-1}+q^{-1}=1/(pq)\), and \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{OA}}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widetilde A_i\)

items.label: Assumption A-1
items.nl: The infinite subject sequence \(\{(Y_i(0),Y_i(1),W_i):i\ge1\}\) is independent and identically distributed, equivalently every \(n\ge1\) prefix is jointly independent with a common law, with the zero-based formal index \(i\in\mathbb N\) obtained by the relabeling \(i\leftrightarrow i+1\).

items.label: Assumption A-9
items.nl: \(Q_i(A\mid x,h)\le \exp(\varepsilon)Q_i(A\mid x',h)\) for every \(i\), \(A\in\mathcal G_i\), \(x,x'\in\mathcal X\), and every history tuple \(h\in\prod_{j<i}\mathcal Z_j\), including null or otherwise unattainable histories in the full history product.

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: For every stationary \(\varepsilon\)-LDP channel \(Q\) from \(\mathcal X\) to an arbitrary measurable output space, there exists a measurable staircase refinement \(Q_\alpha\) with \(\alpha\in\mathcal A_\varepsilon\) such that \(I_\theta(\alpha)\succeq I_\theta(Q)\). Equality in the direction \(v(t)\) permits two active staircase rays \(S\) and \(T\) to be merged only when \(\rho_S(\theta,t)=\rho_T(\theta,t)\) in \(\mathbb R\).

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: For every interior \((\theta,p)\) and fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\inf_Q c^{\top}I_\theta(Q)^{+}c=V^*(\theta,p,\varepsilon)\), with the convention \(+\infty\) when \(c\notin\operatorname{range}(I_\theta(Q))\), and \[J^*(\theta,p,\varepsilon)=\min_{t\in\mathbb R}\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_\varepsilon}F_\theta(\alpha,t)=\min_{t\in\mathbb R}\max_{\alpha\in\operatorname{vert}(\mathcal A_\varepsilon)}F_\theta(\alpha,t).\] Thus the exact oracle is a finite upper envelope of explicit quadratic functions.

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl: At every interior \((\theta,p,\varepsilon)\), an optimizer of \(J^*(\theta,p,\varepsilon)\) exists with \(\kappa(Q_\alpha)\le5\).

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl: The region \(\mathcal R_5\) is relatively open and nonempty. In particular, for \(\varepsilon=\log3\), \(\mu_0=\mu_1=1/2\), and every \(0<p<1/2\), the unique optimal staircase design has active patterns \(\{S_3,S_4,S_6,S_8,S_9\}\). For every \((p,\mu_0,\mu_1,\varepsilon)\in\mathcal R_5\), at a certifying profiling coordinate \(t\), the five active patterns have pairwise distinct projected scores \(\rho_S(\theta,t)\), and every stationary \(\varepsilon\)-LDP channel attaining \(V^*(\theta,p,\varepsilon)\) satisfies \(\kappa(Q)\ge5\). The case \(p>1/2\) follows by exchanging treatment labels.

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl: The region \(\mathcal R_3\) is relatively open and contains \((p,\mu_0,\mu_1,\varepsilon)=(3/10,1/10,1/10,\log3)\). At that point the unique optimal staircase design uses patterns \(\{S_1,S_6,S_8\}\), each with weight \(1/5\), and \[J^*=441/3994,\qquad V^*=3994/441.\]

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl: Holding \(p=3/10\) and \(\varepsilon=\log3\) fixed, on a neighborhood of \((\mu_0,\mu_1)=(1/2,1/2)\) the unique optimal staircase design has active support \(\{S_3,S_4,S_6,S_8,S_9\}\), while on a neighborhood of \((\mu_0,\mu_1)=(1/10,1/10)\) the unique optimal staircase design has active support \(\{S_1,S_6,S_8\}\). On the first neighborhood every attaining stationary \(\varepsilon\)-LDP channel has at least five outputs and the certified staircase channel attains with exactly five; on the second, every attaining stationary \(\varepsilon\)-LDP channel has at least three outputs and the certified staircase channel attains with exactly three. Hence the minimum stationary output cardinality among attaining channels changes from five to three.

items.label: Theorem T-6
items.nl: If \(p=1/2\) and \(\mu_0+\mu_1=1\), then randomized response applied to \((2W_i-1)(2Y_i-1)\) attains \[V^*(\theta,1/2,\varepsilon)=\coth^2(\varepsilon/2)-\tau^2.\]

items.label: Theorem T-7
items.nl: For every measurable strong-saddle selector in \(\mathrm{def{:}pilot\text{-}estimator}\) and every pilot schedule satisfying \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n/n\to0\), the resulting \(\widehat\tau^*\) is sequentially \(\varepsilon\)-LDP and satisfies \(\mathbb E_\theta[\widehat\tau^*\mid H_{m_n}]=\tau\), \[\sqrt n(\widehat\tau^*-\tau)\rightsquigarrow N\!\left(0,V^*(\theta,p,\varepsilon)\right),\qquad \widehat V^*\overset{p}{\longrightarrow}V^*(\theta,p,\varepsilon).\] For every interior \(\theta_0\), the resulting complete procedure sequence belongs to \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{reg}}_{\varepsilon}(\theta_0)\) with \(L_{\mathcal P}=N(0,V^*(\theta_0,p,\varepsilon))\). Consequently \(\widehat\tau^*\pm z_{1-\gamma/2}\sqrt{\widehat V^*/n}\) has pointwise asymptotic coverage \(1-\gamma\), including at channel-support boundaries.

items.label: Theorem T-8
items.nl:
For the published custom Laplace sample mean,
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{OA}}-\tau)\rightsquigarrow N\!\left(0,V_{\mathrm{OA}}(\theta,p,\varepsilon)\right),
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{OA}}=\mu_1/p+\mu_0/q-\tau^2+2\Delta_A^2/\varepsilon^2.
\]
For every measurable strong-saddle selector in \(\mathrm{def{:}pilot\text{-}estimator}\), there exists an admissible pilot schedule, witnessed by \(m_n=\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor\), for which the asymptotic ratio of the custom-Laplace Wald half-length to that of \(\widehat\tau^*\) is \(\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{OA}}/V^*}\). At \((p,\mu_0,\mu_1,\varepsilon)=(1/2,1/2,1/2,1)\), \(V_{\mathrm{OA}}=34\) while \(V^*=\coth^2(1/2)\), so this proposed interval is strictly shorter.

items.label: Theorem T-9
items.nl:
For every fixed \(p\in(0,1)\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(\theta_0\in(0,1)^2\), arbitrary history-dependent measurable output spaces do not improve the regular local asymptotic squared-error constant:
\[
\inf_{\mathcal P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{reg}}_{\varepsilon}(\theta_0)}\;\lim_{H\to\infty}\;\liminf_{n\to\infty}\;\sup_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,H}(\theta_0)}\mathbb E_{\theta_{n,h}}^{\mathcal P}\!\left[(U_{n,h}^{\mathcal P})^2\right]=V^*(\theta_0,p,\varepsilon).
\]
The lower bound holds even without regularity. For every measurable strong-saddle selector in \(\mathrm{def{:}pilot\text{-}estimator}\), there exists an admissible pilot schedule, witnessed by \(m_n=\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor\), whose private-pilot procedure attains the equality and is regular.
